Using fixed-effect meta-analysis of the discovery and replication GWAS summaries, followed by ov.genetics.cross_trait_coloc, I found 8 shared genetic factors (trait-pair colocalizations with PP.H4 > 0.8) across 3 loci among the 13 metabolite traits in the summary files.

Shared loci and metabolite pairs:
- chr1:75641621-76001954: C6 vs C8 (PP.H4=0.998869, PP.H3=0.001131, shared variants=207)
- chr1:75641621-76001954: C6 vs C8/C2 (PP.H4=0.994938, PP.H3=0.005062, shared variants=207)
- chr1:75641621-76001954: C8 vs C8/C2 (PP.H4=0.993687, PP.H3=0.006313, shared variants=207)
- chr1:75641621-76001954: (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 vs C6 (PP.H4=0.986798, PP.H3=0.013202, shared variants=207)
- chr1:46792547-46927183: C10:1 vs C6DC (PP.H4=0.986110, PP.H3=0.013890, shared variants=22)
- chr1:75641621-76001954: (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 vs C8 (PP.H4=0.982734, PP.H3=0.017266, shared variants=207)
- chr1:75641621-76001954: (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 vs C8/C2 (PP.H4=0.949783, PP.H3=0.050217, shared variants=207)
- chr9:129078980-129215422: C4DC+C5-OH vs C6 (PP.H4=0.937264, PP.H3=0.062714, shared variants=135)

The strongest shared-signal locus was chr1:75641621-76001954, which linked four related traits: C6, C8, C8/C2, and (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10. Within this region, C6/C8, C6/C8/C2, and C8/C8/C2 all shared the same lead variant (1:75663549:T:A), and all six pairwise colocalizations at this locus had PP.H4 between 0.949783 and 0.998869.

The other shared loci were chr1:46792547-46927183 for C10:1 vs C6DC (PP.H4=0.986110) and chr9:129078980-129215422 for C4DC+C5-OH vs C6 (PP.H4=0.937264).

Interpretation: these loci are supported as shared genetic factors because the evidence favors one shared causal signal (high PP.H4) rather than two distinct causal variants in the same region (low PP.H3). The results are strongest for related acylcarnitine traits, suggesting pleiotropic genetic control of connected metabolic readouts.

Limitation: this is a summary-statistics colocalization analysis, so it identifies shared association signals rather than experimentally confirmed causal variants or genes.
